results.title: Division 296 super tax explained (including calculator) - SuperGuide
results.description:
# Division 296 super tax explained (including calculator) - [Total tax on investment earnings](https://www.superguide.com.au/super-booster/super-tax-accounts-3-million#h-total-tax-on-investment-earnings) The package of amendments imposes new tax on investment growth that occurs in super balances above $3 million (Division 296 tax). Division 296 tax comes into effect on 1 July 2026 and will apply to investment earnings earned during 2026–27 and following financial years. ## How is the final tax different from the first proposal? In October 2025, the treasurer Jim Chalmers announced changes to the proposal addressing both areas and new bills were introduced. In the final version, super funds are instead required to report realised earnings for affected members. | Previously announced measure | New measure | |-|-| | Earnings calculated based on **changes in TSB**, adjusted for withdrawals and contributions. | Earnings calculated based on the super funds’ **realised earnings** attributed to members with a TSB above the threshold.
Fund earnings will be based on the fund’s taxable income, with adjustments to remove contributions and include exempt current pension income and capital gains on segregated pension assets. | | $3 million threshold **not indexed**. | $3 million threshold **indexed to the consumer price index (CPI)**.
$10 million threshold **indexed to CPI**. | | Additional tax of **15%** applied to the proportion of earnings corresponding to TSBs above **$3 million** | Two-tiered approach applying:
**15%** additional tax on the proportion of earnings corresponding to the TSB **between $3 million and $10 million**
**25%** additional tax on the proportion of earnings corresponding to TSBs **above $10 million** | | Start date **1 July 2025** (focusing on TSB at 30 June 2026) | Start date **1 July 2026** (focusing on TSB at 30 June 2027) | ## Who does it apply to? Division 296 tax applies to the taxable super earnings of individuals whose [total super balance](https://www.superguide.com.au/super-booster/total-superannuation-balance-tsb) (TSB) exceeds $3 million. In 2026–27 (the first year), the tax will be applied based on the TSB at the end of the financial year (30 June 2027). In future financial years, the higher of the TSB on the previous 30 June and year end TSB will be used. From 1 July 2027 onwards, withdrawing super during the financial year will not necessarily prevent Division 296 tax from applying for that year, as balances both immediately prior to the start of the financial year and the end of the financial year are taken into account. ## Collection of the tax In a small concession, the interest rate applied to late payments is four percentage points lower than the rate that applies to most other overdue tax payments. ## Exceptions Earnings from constitutionally protected (untaxed) funds for state higher level office holders, along with earnings from the super of sitting Justices of the High Court appointed before 1 July 2025 and earnings from non-complying funds are exempt from tax.

# $3 million super tax (Division 296 Tax)
## What is the Division 296 Tax?
#### Who will be affected by Division 296 Tax?
The Division 296 Tax will apply if an individual’s TSB before the start or at the end of the financial year is above $3 million and their superannuation earnings are more than nil.

- Individuals with high superannuation balances (i.e. exceeding or soon likely to exceed $3 million) across all phases (accumulation and retirement) may be impacted.

#### For small superannuation funds (SMSFs and SAFs) and larger superannuation funds
This provision will allow small superannuation funds, such as a self-managed superannuation fund (SMSF) or a small APRA fund (SAF) to elect to adjust the cost base of the fund’s CGT assets that it held on 30 June 2026 to the market value of those assets on that day.
